estimate_unit: focused engineer-weeks; 5 working days per engineer-week

phases.title: Technical feasibility and reuse
phases.outcome: Choose a proven implementation path before committing to the graphics and storage stack.

work_packages.description: Timebox SP-00: build and audit an identified OpenToonz revision; record reusable components and coupling, with no automatic whole-application fork.
Run SP-01/02/03/04/05: tablet traces, CPU/GPU rendering, crash-safe storage, vector region topology and rational audio time.
Run SP-06/07 at prototype scale: deformation feasibility and redistributable packages; benchmark the Qt Quick docking candidate.

acceptance: Record hardware, dependency revisions, build flags, licenses and raw measurements.
Select one primary renderer and one fallback; prove a pressure-sensitive stroke on each target OS.
Interrupt every save boundary without publishing missing blobs; demonstrate a viable fill and curve deformation.

Accept or reject each spike with an ADR. Only an unresolved contract used by a delivery slice blocks that slice; unrelated device, fill, docking and renderer-comparison gates remain required for full phase completion.
risks: Renderer interoperability; tablet drivers; topology correctness.

phases.title: Application foundation and English design system
phases.outcome: Open a real local document in a minimal English desktop shell with reversible edits and safe recovery.

work_packages.description: Create CMake/Ninja targets, Conan lockfiles, module boundaries, CI builds and sanitizer profiles; build an English contributor guide.
Implement stable IDs, rational time, command transactions, immutable render snapshots, SQLite/blob storage, migrations and recovery.

Create monochrome QML tokens, keyboard commands, focus rules, dock layout persistence and accessible English strings; audit the English glossary against command IDs, built-in assets and documentation.

acceptance: Create/save/reopen a scene and undo/redo document configuration changes through the real command API.
Simulate disk-full and termination; recover the last committed revision with actionable English errors.
Build on Windows/macOS/Linux; run physical tablet smoke checks on available reference hardware and explicitly mark untested device profiles.
Inventory all visible strings, accessibility labels and first-party docs; English is the release language and non-Latin user text round-trips.
deliverables: Modular desktop shell and headless test target
Versioned project format draft and recovery protocol
English glossary, UI tokens and dependency notices
risks: Premature framework design; docking Qt Quick maturity; inconsistent terminology across product surfaces.

phases.title: First complete frame-by-frame film
phases.outcome: An animator can draw a two-second bouncing ball, save it, reopen it and export 48 PNG frames.

work_packages.description: Implement pencil strokes, pressure width, erasing, selection and stable palette references on vector drawings.
Connect drawing exposures, simple layers, onion skin and playback to the shared time model; use a minimal ordered compositor with alpha-over.
Add still-image import and cancellable PNG sequence export using the same scene evaluator as preview.

acceptance: Complete WF-01 at 1080p/24fps without editing files outside the app; exactly 48 correctly numbered frames export.
Undo a complete stroke, exposure edit and layer reorder; save/reopen retains semantic equality.
Measure B0 tablet latency, pressure fidelity and display scaling on the declared device matrix.
Rerender the reopened scene and compare pixels within the documented backend tolerance; preview and export agree on framing.
deliverables: First user manual and recorded workflow
risks: Stable fill/erase topology and interactive latency.

phases.title: Timeline, Xsheet and paperless workflow
phases.outcome: Animate longer scenes using consistent timeline and Xsheet exposure editing.

work_packages.description: Implement interval-based holds, insert/delete, cycles, timing on twos/threes, stretch and multi-range copy; virtualize timeline and Xsheet views.
Add advanced onion skin, shift-and-trace, flip/desk views, thumbnails, drawing marks and registration tools.
Extend workspace, shortcut, layer grouping, clone/sync, annotations and element management without duplicating document state.

acceptance: Perform equivalent edits in timeline and Xsheet and obtain identical exposure intervals after undo/reopen.
Edit a sparse 10,000-frame scene without allocating a UI item for every cell.
Complete WF-02 rough-to-cleanup using the supported vector subset; preserve registration.
Test keyboard-only editing, focused shortcuts and multi-selection across collapsed groups.
deliverables: Shared exposure editor with two synchronized views
risks: Interval boundary errors; accidental drawing sharing versus duplication.

phases.title: Professional vector drawing and palette workflow
phases.outcome: Clean up and recolor production drawings using editable vector geometry and linked palettes.

work_packages.description: Add region-aware fills, gap closing, invisible strokes, contour/centerline editing, width profiles, cutter, smoothing and curve primitives.
Implement vector brushes, gradient/texture fills, drawing deformation tools, guides, stamps and outline-safe text; retain editable text metadata where supported.
Add four art layers, color models, palette variants, palette repair and multi-drawing operations; explicitly define drawing sharing semantics.

acceptance: Complete WF-02 and WF-03 with recoloring propagated by stable swatch IDs.
Exercise self-intersections, near-coincident curves and small gaps; undo never drops unrelated contours.
Transform or cut a selection without silently converting all vectors to raster.
Preserve all art-layer and palette relations across save, clone and import/export; record tolerances for curve flattening.
deliverables: Vector editing and fill topology specification
risks: Polygon libraries do not solve editable curve topology automatically.

phases.title: Raster and textured brush engine
phases.outcome: Mix tiled bitmap artwork and vector drawings with responsive textured brushes.

work_packages.description: Integrate libmypaint through a brush/tile adapter; benchmark color conversion, stroke sampling and undo tile diffs.
Implement bitmap layers, selection, resolution changes, texture-backed vector brushes/pencils and deterministic preset serialization.
Evaluate an ABR subset importer with explicit compatibility reporting; preserve original presets and reject unsupported variants safely.

acceptance: Paint B3 at 4K with bounded tiles/caches and cancellable operations; report cold/warm memory separately.
Compare undo/reopen stroke output and pressure transitions using recorded input streams.
Import documented ABR fixtures or publish precise unsupported fields; do not claim general Photoshop brush compatibility.
Mix raster and vectors while keeping premultiplication and color transforms consistent.
deliverables: ABR support matrix and memory benchmark
risks: Brush engine surface format, ABR coverage and excessive tile snapshots.

phases.title: Keyframe animation and multiplane cameras
phases.outcome: Animate transform hierarchies and camera moves with predictable timing and curves.

work_packages.description: Implement setup/animate modes, pegs, pivots, transform channels, stepped/continuous keys, autokey and batched key editing.
Build curve/ease and motion-path editors with explicit interpolation, velocity and extrapolation semantics.
Add multiple cameras, animated orthographic framing, multiplane Z, staging views and reusable motion transfers; 3D views here show 2D planes, not imported meshes.

acceptance: Animate a camera move and character hierarchy; reopening preserves all evaluated keyframe values.
Verify parent-child transforms and pivot edits with nonuniform scale and negative scale.
Scrub and export identical camera framing at integer and rational frame rates.
Copy and retime key ranges without changing unrelated channels; undo restores the complete edit.
risks: Coordinate spaces, rotation interpolation and setup-versus-animation state.

phases.title: Sound and practical media output
phases.outcome: Edit dialogue against drawings and deliver synchronized image or movie output.

work_packages.description: Use miniaudio for device playback/mixing and a restricted FFmpeg adapter for decoding/encoding; keep one authoritative rational timeline clock.
Add waveforms, trim/offset, gain, scrub, audio library, preview quality and render-range controls.

Add video import, video/audio export, GIF and standalone playback; distinguish input decoding support from redistributable output codec profiles. Deliver manual viseme mapping/correction after character substitution contracts; evaluate automatic detection separately after manual editing works.

acceptance: Play and export a ten-minute rational-rate scene with audiovisual drift within NFR-007.
Cancel render and device changes cleanly; no partial output is reported as complete.
Check waveform, trim and gain against a known waveform and exact sample boundaries.
Install the minimal licensed media build on clean target systems and list available codecs at runtime.
Complete WF-07 after the character substitution subset, preserving manual corrections and flagging unmapped labels; English and Spanish detector evaluations remain distinct.
risks: Real-time thread allocations, device loss and build-dependent codec licensing.

phases.title: Character assets, substitutions and accessible rig controls
phases.outcome: Build reusable characters with first-class parts, substitutions, poses and declarative controls; guide initial setup through an editable Quick Rig recipe.

work_packages.description: Implement breakdown, hierarchy editing, pivots, Z ordering, substitutions, pose copying and patching seams.
Create versioned local libraries, templates, symbols, previews and paste modes; instantiate assets without accidental shared edits.
Implement saved partial poses, canvas widgets, one-dimensional pose sliders, mapping and compact character dashboards with stable portable bindings; no scripting prerequisite.
Deliver guided Quick Rig: map named parts, place joint guides, preview/correct FK hierarchy and controls, then commit once; extend recipes to proven deformer/IK capabilities only after their gates.

acceptance: Complete WF-04 with a reusable waving character and independently editable instances.
Reimport a rig template without ID collisions or lost palette dependencies.
Capture/apply a masked pose and switch coordinated substitutions without changing unrelated animation.
Create/cancel/undo Quick Rig, then edit the same document in the full rig workspace; two template instances have independent bindings.
Declarative controls remain usable without Python; advanced scripted controls belong to P12.
risks: Symbol ownership and mouth-drawing mapping; detector quality varies by language.
phases.milestone: Reusable character authoring; Harmony Moment core subsets first

phases.title: Core deformation
phases.outcome: Animate curved limbs and flexible drawings with stable rest poses and attachments.

work_packages.description: Implement bone, curve and envelope evaluation over an explicit rest-space mesh with consistent texture coordinates. Extract rest-space binding and bounded renderer-backed mesh/texture feasibility before the full phase; do not require region-fill completion for registered alpha artwork.
Add influence editing, multiple poses, generated envelopes and deformation quality/visibility controls.

Implement kinematic attachments and bake-to-drawings with provenance and bounded approximation error. Add a bounded two-bone IK subset with limits, explicit solve order and unreachable-target behavior; multi-pin constraints remain in P13.

acceptance: Complete WF-05 and compare rest, posed and baked drawings within declared tolerances.
Test joints, folds and extreme poses on B4 with a checker texture; reject invalid weights predictably.
Animation remains reproducible after reopen and template reuse.
Profile interactive edits separately from final render; expose quality settings without changing saved intent.
deliverables: Rig fixtures and bake accuracy report
risks: Self-intersections, mesh quality and numerical conditioning.

phases.title: Node compositor and managed color
phases.outcome: Compose scenes with editable node graphs, masks, effects and consistent color-managed output.

work_packages.description: Promote the early ordered compositor to a typed acyclic graph with groups, switches, viewer/output nodes and dirty propagation; migrate old projects.
Build the node editor as a view over the document graph; implement basic blending, opacity, blur, glow, shadows, color correction and mattes.
Integrate OpenColorIO and HDR-capable image IO, define working/display/output transforms and add multi-output/headless rendering.

acceptance: Complete the supported 2D subset of WF-08 with masks, camera movement and multiple outputs.
Validate cycles, incompatible ports and missing assets before render with English node-specific diagnostics.
Use B5 charts to verify alpha, linear-light composition and display/export transforms.
Change one upstream parameter and show correct selective invalidation; render the same revision through UI and CLI.
deliverables: Typed compositor and node operator contract
risks: Graph migration, color-space errors and GPU/CPU consistency.

phases.title: Reliable 1.0 release
phases.outcome: Ship a dependable supported offline 2D 1.0 after the complete phase gates; qualify the narrower Harmony Moment workflow earlier without claiming P11 completion.

work_packages.description: Run complete drawing, cut-out, audio and 2D compositing journeys with animators; prioritize data-loss and workflow blockers over new tools.
Complete project compaction, revision/history, optimization and recovery UX; finalize format migration and supported OS/device profiles.
Produce installable packages, dependency notices/SBOM, English help, accessibility review and reproducible release evidence; test installation and upgrades.

acceptance: Complete WF-01 through WF-05, WF-07, the supported 2D part of WF-08 and WF-12 on the published matrix.
No known data-loss defect or critical release blocker remains; all relevant NFR budgets are measured or explicitly narrowed before release.
Open all earlier release fixtures or issue a recoverable migration diagnostic; backup before destructive migration.
Publish an accurate support matrix: advanced controllers/morph/3D/studio/AI are later releases, not implied by the 1.0 label.
deliverables: English user/contributor docs and measured support matrix
risks: Polish and compatibility debt; premature claims of feature completeness.

phases.title: Automation and extension foundations
phases.outcome: Automate editing and rendering through a documented, versioned command API.

work_packages.description: Expose stable document queries and transactions through a C++ application API and pybind11 Python bindings. Scripted controllers (CTL-006) depend on the versioned extension boundary; declarative character controls do not.
Build script editor, custom actions, explicit trusted-script permissions and a separate process for restricted automation; Python bindings themselves are not a sandbox.
Add CLI batch jobs, deterministic expression evaluation, cancellation, version negotiation and plugin manifests.

acceptance: A script generates and renders a scene using the same validated commands and undo rules as the UI.
Reject unsupported API versions with a migration hint; never execute scripts embedded in a project automatically.
A terminated worker leaves no partial document transaction or completed-looking output.
Document which scripts are trusted and which restrictions are enforced by OS process boundaries, not a misleading restricted Python namespace.
risks: ABI stability, trust boundaries and expression nondeterminism.

phases.title: Advanced constraints, pose grids and deformation controls
phases.outcome: Build sophisticated reusable character controls and layered deformation rigs.

work_packages.description: Extend the core two-bone IK solver to multi-chain constraints, nails and animated constraint transitions with explicit solve order; add the Breakdown Assistant.
Add free-form, shape-aware and weighted deformations plus deform-on-deform composition; evaluate selected Eigen/libigl solvers.
Extend declarative controllers with two-dimensional pose grids and deformer-on-deformer composition; custom scripting uses P12, while ordinary widgets/sliders/dashboard/templates are owned by P08.

acceptance: Complete WF-06 with a 60-control rig, mirrored poses and combined substitutions/deformations.
Test unreachable IK targets and degenerate weighted meshes without NaNs or corrupted saved data.
Controller mappings round-trip through templates and behave consistently with direct channel editing.
Measure solve cost during interaction and final render; document approximation and influence limits per solver.
deliverables: Advanced rig examples and solver reports
risks: Solver stability, dependency ordering and opaque controller behavior.

phases.title: Morphing and drawing interpolation
phases.outcome: Interpolate compatible drawings with artist-controlled correspondences.

work_packages.description: Define compatibility rules for contour topology, art layers, palette references and holes.
Implement correspondence hints, intermediate keys, timing and preview; preserve source drawings and derived results separately.
Add explicit diagnostics and bake options for unsupported topology changes and raster content.

acceptance: Complete shape interpolation fixtures with holes and alpha without losing contour identity.
An incompatible pair reports actionable reasons instead of silently producing a broken drawing.
Hint editing is reversible and deterministic across save/reopen.
Compare endpoints exactly and intermediates against approved animation references with bounded geometric error.
risks: Topology changes and correspondence ambiguities.

phases.title: Advanced effects, particles and OpenFX
phases.outcome: Create procedural effects and particle scenes inside the managed compositor.

work_packages.description: Add remaining filters, channel operations, generated mattes, texture animation, distortions and surface/normal lighting.
Build a seeded particle simulation with emitters, forces, collisions, lifecycle, caches and versioned baked results.
Evaluate OpenFX host support in an isolated worker with explicit supported suites, capabilities and plugin license records.

acceptance: Rerender seeded particles identically on the supported deterministic path; timeline jumps use valid simulation state.
Test out-of-frame regions, premultiplied alpha, HDR values and tiled boundaries for every added effect.
A crashing or incompatible external plugin reports failure without damaging the project.
Benchmark B3/B5 memory and cancellation, and publish operator-specific tolerances and OpenFX compatibility.
risks: Simulation determinism, expensive effect chains and third-party plugin behavior.

phases.title: Production interchange
phases.outcome: Exchange layered artwork, editorial timing and compositing results with external tools.

work_packages.description: Add layered PSD import/export with explicit layer/mask/blend subsets; evaluate PSD-specific tooling where generic image IO cannot preserve layers.
Implement vector interchange, linked image updates, scan/vectorization workflow and OTIO timeline mapping.
Add editorial and After Effects-oriented interchange adapters with exact supported schemas, conversion reports and portable references.

acceptance: Round-trip redistributable layered/vector fixtures and list every unsupported construct; no blanket lossless claim.
Changing a linked image creates a controlled revision and can be undone or reverted.
Import editorial timing at rational rates without silently shifting audio or exposures.
Render comparison fixtures for downstream exchange and document version-specific limitations.
risks: Format semantics, external version drift and unsupported PSD/AE constructs.

phases.title: Mixed 2D and 3D scenes
phases.outcome: Integrate imported 3D assets into a controlled 2D animation workflow.

work_packages.description: Evaluate ufbx/fastgltf import adapters, coordinate/unit conversions, materials, hierarchy, skinning and animation clips.
Add 3D subnode visibility/overrides, normalized depth and compositing with 2D planes through a declared renderer contract.
Add an optional external-render bridge with versioned job manifests and portable asset references.

acceptance: Complete WF-09 using redistributable models with known units, skin weights and animated clips.
Compare axis/handedness and camera projections with reference transforms; texture paths remain portable.
Document which material/shader features are mapped, approximated or unsupported.
GPU failure or external renderer failure yields recoverable job errors and preserves editable 2D work.
risks: Material parity, 3D GPU complexity and import format edge cases.

phases.title: Game animation export
phases.outcome: Deliver predictable sprite and skeletal assets to a documented open runtime.

work_packages.description: Implement atlas packing, variants, anchors/collision metadata and effects baking with deterministic frame bounds.
Add game-oriented bones and an independently documented animation runtime format; avoid dependence on proprietary SDKs.
Build a minimal open reference runtime and import example; define runtime skinning, color and interpolation support.

acceptance: Complete WF-10 and compare runtime playback with baked reference frames.
Verify atlas padding, rotated regions, trim offsets and transparent borders at multiple scales.
Report unsupported rig/effect behavior and offer a bake fallback with size estimates.
Version the exported schema and test a previous exporter version against the runtime.
deliverables: Open runtime schema and example player
risks: Runtime parity, shader constraints and asset size.

phases.title: Studio coordination and render queues
phases.outcome: Coordinate shared productions while preserving reliable offline scene ownership.

work_packages.description: Model productions, roles, asset checkout, scene/drawing locks and lease recovery with explicit conflict semantics.
Add revision comparison and limited semantic merges; keep unresolved artistic conflicts visible instead of overwriting them.
Build idempotent render queue workers, shared storage adapters and role-specific Paint/Scan workspaces.

acceptance: Complete WF-11 under concurrent edits, network loss and expired leases; no silent last-writer data loss.
A requeued render job cannot publish conflicting outputs for one revision.
Audit access and lock state using English diagnostics; offline checkout remains usable under documented rules.
Test backup/restore, migrations and worker version skew in a small real production pilot.
deliverables: Optional studio services and deployment guide
risks: Distributed state, merge ambiguity and operational cost.

phases.title: Optional local AI tools
phases.outcome: Offer opt-in assistive image operations with explicit model provenance and reversible results.

work_packages.description: Evaluate ONNX Runtime and redistribution-compatible models for masks, erase, outpaint, upscale and fill separately.
Implement cancellable worker jobs, model/download manifests, resource budgets and preview/apply through document transactions.
Provide offline operation after optional model installation, clear generated-content provenance and quality comparisons with manual workflows.

acceptance: The editor installs, opens, draws and exports without any model, login or network service.
Every enabled operation has a usable licensed model, evaluated visual quality and explicit memory/hardware requirements.
Cancel or reject a generated result without changing source artwork; applying it is undoable.
No user artwork is uploaded by default; any later remote adapter requires a separately explicit action and disclosure.
deliverables: Optional AI worker and model registry
risks: Usable model licenses, artifacts and large downloads; runtime alone supplies no models.

phases.title: Legacy migration adapters
phases.outcome: Provide isolated legacy conversion where technically viable and worthwhile.

work_packages.description: Investigate FLA/SWF input and EaselJS export with redistributable fixtures and current parser/runtime maintenance evidence.
Implement supported static/timeline subsets behind optional adapters or a documented external conversion path.
Publish exact conversion losses and record an explicit deferred disposition for unsupported executable or proprietary constructs.

acceptance: Each legacy requirement has a tested supported subset or a documented deferred decision; a deferred item remains unimplemented.
No active legacy content is executed merely to inspect or import a file.
Malformed and oversized inputs are bounded and isolated.
Reference animations compare before/after in a maintained viewer or reproducible fixture pipeline.
risks: Obsolete formats, active content and low maintenance value.

phases.title: Coverage audit and long-term maintenance
phases.outcome: Publish evidence of actual capability coverage and sustain the application across releases.

work_packages.description: Audit all 283 feature records and all 193 node-reference entries; expand family entries into concrete operators/properties before claiming parity.
Run end-to-end artistic workflows, dependency upgrades, format migration history and supported platform/device regression suites.
Publish verified/partial/deferred coverage, maintenance ownership, support policy and the next evidence-driven roadmap.

acceptance: Every feature and node reference has an accountable disposition and linked evidence; counts alone never certify parity.
Optional or legacy deferrals are visible and do not block maintenance releases of the core editor.
Retained project fixtures survive supported upgrades; retired platforms/formats have documented migration paths.
Release notes and public claims match measured functionality, including limitations and unresolved gaps.
risks: Documentation drift and unfunded maintenance.

delivery_slices.title: Reference shot and foundation decisions
delivery_slices.scope: Freeze the bounded character-shot profile, failure fixtures and only the contracts needed by its next consumers. Audit current code instead of restarting all feasibility work.
acceptance: Record a redistributable 20-second 1080p/24fps character shot, a 24000/1001 variant and a ten-minute audio drift fixture with explicit budgets.

Approve IDs/space/time/color/migration and command-ownership contracts, plus a saved-scene success rubric artistically reviewed by the project owner; record hardware rather than infer performance. Independent working-shot animator validation remains HM-15.
excluded: No blanket renderer rewrite, OpenToonz fork, full tablet matrix, docking framework or fill-topology gate.

delivery_slices.title: Persistent rig properties and typed document contracts

requires.contract: Accepted stable entity/property IDs, transform spaces, rational time and migration policy

delivery_slices.scope: Expose stable typed part/peg/property addresses over the existing full-pose evaluator and Session commands. Preserve the current transform-key representation through a compatibility adapter; introduce discrete or specialized tracks only with their actual character/deformer consumers. Define rest/authored/evaluated ownership and transactional persistence. Character/deformer/audio/node payloads are added by their owning slices, not empty schemas in advance.
acceptance: Existing full-pose keys, easing, visual curve edits and key-block edits retain their sampled behavior through the property-address adapter; reject dangling IDs, invalid types/values and duplicate keys. No wholesale curve-engine rewrite is required.
Version new persisted semantics, back up migrations and fail safely in older readers; undo/save/reopen and injected failures retain all references.
Separate rest/setup values, authored animation, evaluated results and view state; expose one command/query boundary for the UI and evaluator.
excluded: No embedded scripting, arbitrary expressions or general plugin API.
No upfront migration of every legacy transform channel to a new keyframe engine; version only schema changes required by actual consumers.

delivery_slices.title: Registered artwork intake

requires.contract: Defined image origin, alpha, color profile, resource bounds and part-registration fixture

delivery_slices.scope: Qualify existing drawing and still-image import; add ordered PNG sequence intake and registered part intake with explicit sequence-versus-parts choice, missing-frame reports and asset bounds. Existing vector/raster tools supply original artwork.
acceptance: Round-trip original sampled vectors and transparent PNG parts without shifting their registration or changing color IDs.
A failed/cancelled multi-file import leaves no half-created document; sequence gaps and ordering are explicit.
excluded: PSD, SVG, vectorization, advanced brush presets and analytic fill are not required; pre-separated PNG parts are a supported route.

delivery_slices.title: Character identity, pegs and substitution sets

requires.contract: Typed stable part/peg/property IDs and atomic persistence
Validated drawings and registered imported parts

delivery_slices.scope: Create a character root and stable part roles; keep separate transform hierarchy and render order. Add preserve-world reparenting, rest pivots, named thumbnail substitutions, held selector tracks and coordinated variant sets.
acceptance: Build a rigid character and change mouth/hand/view without moving its peg, overwriting transform keys or affecting another character.
Reparent supported negative/nonuniform transforms without registration jumps; reject nonrepresentable shear or singular cases explicitly.
Coordinated variants switch atomically, missing members are reported, and duplicate instances get independent bindings.
excluded: Automatic image segmentation, full library management and deformation are not prerequisites for rigid cut-out.

delivery_slices.title: Shared evaluation and typed graph kernel

requires.contract: Addressed animated properties, immutable snapshots and versioned persistence

delivery_slices.scope: Extract the existing ordered painter into a shared evaluation boundary with typed image/transform/matte inputs, DAG validation, revision invalidation and explicit Display/Write targets. Register operators only with consumers. Use a restricted linear-sRGB premultiplied composition profile and preserve legacy scene appearance through an explicit legacy profile.
acceptance: Known ordered legacy scenes retain their declared appearance on migration; new-profile alpha charts and UI/headless outputs match within recorded tolerance.
Detect cycles, dangling references and incompatible ports; edited upstream properties invalidate descendants and stale jobs cannot publish.
Define solve ordering for property drivers, hierarchy, deformation, attachments, camera and image composition without conflating the transform graph with the image graph.
excluded: No full node editor, large effect catalog, HDR/EXR, OCIO configuration manager or GPU rewrite.

delivery_slices.title: Rest binding and deformation rendering feasibility

requires.contract: Stable part/variant bindings and rest-space transforms
One evaluated geometry/image boundary and explicit alpha/color contract

delivery_slices.scope: Prove the complete bind-to-render route before authoring tools: rest mesh/UVs, editable bind controls and per-substitution binding compatibility. Start with bounded regular meshes over alpha artwork; compare tessellation only if the fixture requires it. Retain editable source vectors and use an explicitly resolution-limited render proxy where needed.
acceptance: Checker artwork survives rest/pose/reset without UV drift, seams or accumulated deformation; benchmark the actual renderer, not only a solver.
Reject degenerate geometry and incompatible substitutions; rebinding reports affected animation rather than silently discarding it.
Choose and pin a proven numerical/render route within the spike budget; if the texture warp cannot meet quality/cost, resolve that blocker before HM-06.
excluded: No claim of native analytic vector deformation; no dependency on full region topology, optimal meshing or libigl weight solvers.

delivery_slices.title: Bone and curve deformers

requires.contract: Accepted rest mesh/UV/binding representation and measured deformation render path

delivery_slices.scope: Deliver editable bone chains and curve chains with defined local/rest spaces, stable weights, predictable joint/tangent behavior and saved animated properties. Controls drag on canvas with cancellable previews; variant changes resolve their own binding.
acceptance: Animate a bent arm and curved torso/tail with rest reset, key interpolation, undo and saved/rendered equivalence.
Extreme bends, zero-length bones and invalid weights give bounded behavior without NaNs or corrupting rest data; proxy resolution limits are visible.
Pass the bounded B4/HM shot quality and interaction budgets; unresolved seam/texture artifacts block the deformer claim.
excluded: Envelope/automatic envelope, free-form, shape-aware and deformer-on-deformer remain long-term requirements.

delivery_slices.title: First-class poses and declarative animator controls

requires.contract: Stable character/part IDs, substitutions and transform properties
Deterministic driver ordering, type checks and cycle rejection

delivery_slices.scope: Save named masked poses including discrete substitutions; apply/mirror only explicitly mapped parts. Add direct widgets, limited sliders/switches and a compact character dashboard. Pose interpolation blends compatible numeric properties; discrete variants use an explicit threshold rule. Animator and Rig workspaces expose the same document at different detail levels.
acceptance: A pose slider reproduces stored numeric and discrete endpoints exactly; applying a pose leaves excluded channels untouched.
A widget edits only its published properties through ordinary commands; conflicting drivers or graph cycles cannot silently win.
An animator can select a character, pose it and switch mouths without opening nodes; a rigger can inspect/edit all bindings in the same project.
excluded: No Python, arbitrary script controllers, 2D pose grids or generic expression engine. Deformer controls activate only after HM-06.

delivery_slices.title: Quick Rig guided FK recipe

requires.contract: Character part/peg ownership and safe preserve-world operations
Published control/pose bindings and animator workspace

delivery_slices.scope: Assign part roles and place joint guides directly on canvas; preview an editable FK hierarchy and control set before one commit. Offer a simple biped recipe and manual correction. Generated rigs use the same model as hand-authored rigs.
acceptance: Create a FK character from registered parts with no manual node wiring; record setup time/actions against the same manual workflow without claiming superiority before measurement.
Cancel/undo is atomic; missing roles, mirrored orientation and repeat-run update versus new-instance choice are explicit.
The full rig view reveals every generated binding; guides never render.
excluded: No AI/auto-segmentation, irreversible bake or unsupported deformer recipe.

delivery_slices.title: Integrated deformable rig, IK and portable templates

requires.contract: Working bone/curve evaluation with per-variant binding
Pose/control mappings and saved driver semantics
Editable guided rig recipe and role mappings

delivery_slices.scope: Add kinematic endpoint/curve attachments, bounded two-bone IK with limits and explicit FK/IK ownership; extend Quick Rig with optional proven limb recipes. Close template dependency collection over parts, swatches, variants, poses, controls, bind data and animation. Use a validated local folder manifest first.
acceptance: A hand/accessory follows a deformed arm without being deformed twice; unreachable targets preserve declared length/limit policy.
Switch variants and apply poses without orphaned deformer links; shared versus independent imports are explicit and two instances animate independently.
Template export/import remaps all IDs, rejects missing resources and includes all registered payload dependencies; later graph/matte payloads extend the same collector before HM-15.
excluded: Multi-pin/nails, animated constraint switching, general IK networks, live template updates and archive transport are later.

delivery_slices.title: Audio clock, waveform and manual timing

requires.contract: Saved typed audio assets/clips, rational sample/frame conversion and cancellable snapshot jobs

delivery_slices.scope: Adopt one playback backend after the miniaudio spike; start with WAV/PCM, waveform pyramids, trim/offset/gain, limited mixing and frame scrub. Audio device time drives playback, while headless sampling uses the same rational scene mapping.
acceptance: Ten-minute 24 and 24000/1001 scenes stay within one-frame accumulated audiovisual drift; report underruns and dropped preview frames.
Seek, loop, pause, device loss and sample-rate conversion do not desynchronize the playhead or mutate media; waveform peaks align with sample positions.
Audio references, edits and original asset hashes survive undo/reopen; callbacks avoid document locks/allocations.
excluded: No raster/vector completion, lip detector, FFmpeg codec catalog or audio recording prerequisite.

delivery_slices.title: Mouth mapping and editable lip sync

requires.contract: Named mouth substitution IDs and held selector track
Audio time mapping, waveform and frame scrub

delivery_slices.scope: Map a small labelled viseme set to each character and edit held mouth timings against audio. Import a documented timing JSON with rational conversion and previewed merge ranges; preserve manual corrections.
acceptance: Complete English and Spanish dialogue by hand; flag unmapped labels and retain corrections through retiming, save/reopen and export.
Imported labels cannot overwrite unrelated or protected manual timings; gaps, overlaps and clip offsets have explicit rules.
excluded: Automatic recognition is a follow-on enhancement, not a dependency of reliable lip-sync editing.

delivery_slices.title: Useful nodes, cutters and part overlap

requires.contract: Typed graph runtime, color/alpha and shared output evaluator
Character group and separate hierarchy/render-order identity

delivery_slices.scope: Expose a small editable node graph: Drawing, Peg/Transform, ordered Composite, Opacity, Cutter/Matte, group ports, Display and Write. Add reversible front/back part ordering and manual joint matte recipes; a compact inspector hides graph complexity from animators.
acceptance: Animate an arm crossing the torso and mask an eye/joint with fractional alpha; group/ungroup and bypass preserve intended pixels and references.
Graph edits reject incompatible ports/cycles and undo atomically; a matte is not treated as binary.
The template dependency collector includes graph and matte resources; deleting referenced nodes cannot silently leave a partial rig.
excluded: No automatic Auto Patch topology, general Z/multiplane, effects catalog, OpenFX or full node inventory.

delivery_slices.title: Output camera and framing

requires.contract: Shared evaluator, addressed transform properties and scene-to-output boundary

delivery_slices.scope: Add an explicit active orthographic output camera with animated pan/zoom/rotation and nonrendering framing guides. Separate camera edits from canvas navigation; retain drawing-local coordinates.
acceptance: A camera move yields identical framing in preview, reopened scene and PNG export; viewport pan/zoom never changes exported composition.
Camera keys interpolate with existing animation semantics, and invalid/singular framing fails clearly.
excluded: Multiplane parallax, perspective/3D staging views and camera switching UI are post-milestone.

delivery_slices.title: Synchronized preview and deterministic delivery

requires.contract: Authoritative audio clock and exact scene-to-sample mapping
Evaluated node/matte composition and distinct Display/Write
Output-camera sampling shared by preview/export

delivery_slices.scope: Preview the bounded shot from revision-keyed caches with visible dropped-frame/quality state. Export an exact-range PNG sequence plus synchronized PCM WAV and an explicit timing/color manifest; save/reopen the same immutable revision before comparing output.
acceptance: Deliver every expected frame and sample interval at 24 and 24000/1001 with declared endpoint rounding; cancellation never reports complete output.

UI, reopened and headless outputs agree for baseline drawing, camera and node/matte composition; late jobs cannot replace newer results. Deformer/rig combinations join the complete export regression at HM-15 after HM-09, without blocking this independent output slice.
PNG plus WAV is the mandatory open delivery profile. Movie encoding is explicitly the next output extension after the milestone, not an implied capability.
excluded: No codec catalog, HDR/EXR/multi-pass, video reference import or distributed render queue gate.

delivery_slices.title: Harmony Moment reliability and artist acceptance

requires.contract: Reusable deformable character with functioning controls, attachments and template closure
Editable dialogue/mouth timing
Camera/node preview and synchronized deterministic output

delivery_slices.scope: Run the complete original-art and imported-parts routes on the declared Mac profile: create character, variants, Quick Rig, bone/curve edits, poses/IK, dialogue, cutters, camera move, preview, save/reopen and export. Reuse the character in a second scene and exercise failures; this is a bounded workflow milestone before full P11/1.0.
acceptance: An animator other than the implementer completes both 20-second shot routes using the guide, without manual JSON repair or developer assistance; record blockers and setup/pose correction time.
No known data-loss or critical workflow blocker; undo/redo, crash recovery, missing assets and legacy migration retain recoverable project/rig state.

Reopened outputs match; template reuse remaps controls, bind variants, graph/matte and media references completely. Pass published frame/latency/memory budgets for the fixture, without claiming all catalog NFRs.
Record Mac hardware, exact dependencies/notices and limitations. Physical tablets and wider OS/install qualification remain explicit open gates; publication is a separate owner decision.
excluded: Not Harmony parity, full phase completion or a supported cross-platform 1.0.

execution_policy.primary_objective: HM: reliable character animation Harmony Moment
execution_policy.current_instruction: HM-01 and HM-02 bounded contracts are accepted. Continue HM-03 rigid character work: thumbnail substitutions, coordinated view sets and instance-safe duplication before claiming HM-03 complete. HM-04 and HM-10 are independently eligible but require separate bounded ownership.
execution_policy.phase_dependency_semantics: Phase depends_on constrains full epic completion, not entry into an implementation slice. Only the explicit delivery-slice contract DAG gates the Harmony Moment. Domain dependencies are scope relationships, not all-features barriers.
execution_policy.entry_rule: Start a slice only when each required contract has accepted evidence. Baseline reuse is partial and must be qualified; planned is not ready. Independent spikes may run without claiming their consumer ready.
execution_policy.staffing: One integration owner; at most two bounded slices with distinct owners when people are available. For one implementer, follow priority_order sequentially.
execution_policy.full_phase_closure: After HM-15, close retained P00-P11 scope/qualification for 1.0; do not erase unimplemented requirements to claim completion.

harmony_moment.title: Harmony Moment: reusable speaking character shot

profile.platform: macOS development profile; exact hardware recorded in HM-00
profile.artwork: Original sampled vector/raster artwork and registered transparent PNG parts; no PSD/SVG prerequisite
profile.shot: 20 seconds, 1920x1080, 24fps plus 24000/1001 variant; one 12-20-part character, 8 mouth variants, 3 hands, 2 coordinated views, 2 bone/curve chains, 1 attachment, 12 published controls, 2 audio clips, 3 mattes and 1 orthographic camera
profile.delivery: PNG sequence + PCM WAV + timing/color manifest; review movie encoding follows HM
profile.audio_budget: NFR-007 one-frame maximum drift over ten minutes; waveform/scrub aligns within one displayed frame
profile.proposed_interaction_budget: On recorded hardware, cached 1080p/24fps preview; p95 control-to-preview <=50 ms at declared preview quality; resident memory <=2 GiB for the fixture. Proposed acceptance targets, not current measurements. Recalibration requires an explicit scope/quality decision.
profile.correctness: No unresolved data loss/critical workflow defect; legacy migrations backed up, rig IDs portable, deterministic reopened exports, artistic acceptance required

not_claimed: Harmony file compatibility or full feature parity
Physical tablet, Intel, Linux/Windows or clean-machine qualification
Measured superiority over Harmony before comparative artist study

estimate_revision.basis: Whole-program phase envelopes retain prior scope and are not estimates of remaining HM work. HM slice estimates cover remaining bounded work once, including integration; never add them to phase totals.
changes: Move declarative controls/guides from P13 to P08: 6-10 engineer-weeks transferred.
Move core IK from P13 to P09: 2-4 transferred; move scripted controller from P13 to P12: 2-4 transferred.
Move lip-sync ownership from P08 to P07: 2-4 transferred.
Add distinct Quick Rig capability to P08: 3-6 additional whole-program engineer-weeks.
estimate_revision.confidence: Low. Re-estimate after HM-01 and the renderer-backed HM-05 spike; no calendar commitment.
